transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-25 15:00 UTC - Duration 55m - Recording id ff-20250625-7c9b2
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Product), Priya Rao (Lumina Director of ML), Michael Chen (Lumina Infra), Sofia Alvarez (Lumina PM)
Artifacts referenced: cutover-runbook-draft (link), canary-metrics-sheet (link), staging-smoke-tests.md (link), SOC2-and-security.pdf (link)

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the Week 4 pilot sync. Quick check - agenda is 1) run through proposed cutover runbook, 2) canary/A-B plan, 3) monitoring and rollback criteria, 4) next steps. Anything to add?
[00:18] Priya: No, that's good. Want to make sure we get the canary window locked down today.
[00:24] Michael: Also need to confirm firewall/credentials for the private deployment test.
[00:30] Samir: Great, I'll share the runbook link in the chat now. It's the draft with the smoke-test steps and the metric thresholds pre-populated.
[00:45] Jordan: Quick FYI - we've updated the recommended canary thresholds after last week's perf run, lower latency threshold and more conservative error-rate ceiling.
[01:12] Priya: Cool, can you call out the thresholds? I didn't open the doc yet.
[01:20] Samir: Sure. For the canary we're proposing a 4-hour window at 5% traffic, with a 99th percentile latency SLO of 450ms and error-rate threshold of 0.8%. If either threshold breaches for 3 consecutive 5-minute buckets we auto-fail the canary.
[01:47] Michael: 0.8% is tight for our spikes. What's the rollback plan if it breaches?
[01:54] Ava: The runbook lists immediate rollback to hosted fallback (Redwood-hosted replica) and re-route via smart routing. We have scripted rollback commands in section 4.3. If automatic rollback fails, SE will execute manual revert and the on-call infra performs full traffic cut.
[02:20] Priya: Is the hosted fallback compatible with our data residency needs? We had flagged EU-only for PHI.
[02:28] Jordan: Yes, for Lumina we recommend a region-bound hosted fallback in eu-west-1 to meet residency. The fallback does not persist customer data beyond session scope—it's a stateless execution for the canary.
[02:50] Sofia: Quick question — do we need a maintenance window? The ask from ops was a 2-hour blackout for DB schema work same day.
[02:58] Ava: Good catch. We should avoid overlapping maintenance. Proposed cutover is 03-July at 02:00 UTC with a four-hour canary to follow. That avoids your DB work per earlier schedule.
[03:20] Priya: 03-July works for execs. Can we shorten the canary if metrics look good?
[03:26] Samir: Yes, we can do early promotion at 50% reduction of risk: if no threshold violations and token cost/latency trends are stable for first 90 minutes, we can extend traffic to 25% and reassess. But any extension must still hit the final health checks.
[03:50] Michael: What health checks are those specifically?
[04:00] Samir: A mix: API success rate >99.2%, 95th p95 latency <300ms, memory/KV cache evictions <1%, and telemetry showing steady request per second. We also check downstream service error logs—if dependent services spike we pause.
[04:25] Priya: Do you have dashboard screenshots?
[04:28] Samir: Yes, in the canary-metrics-sheet link — I added a staging dashboard that mirrors prod telemetry. We'll invite your SREs to it.
[04:40] Priya: Please invite Michael and our on-call rotation.
[04:44] Michael: Yes please. Also we need the bastion host creds and CIDR for Redwood Private so we can open firewall rules.
[04:52] Ava: We'll include templated firewall rules in the runbook. Samir, can you inline the CIDR and bastion steps?
[04:59] Samir: On it. The runbook has the commands but I'll add sample iptables and AWS security-group snippets.
[05:10] Sofia: Back to rollback — who does the actual traffic cut if automatic fallback doesn't trigger?
[05:16] Ava: Primary: Redwood SE (Samir) executes the runbook rollback. Secondary: Lumina infra (Michael) has network-level cutover authority to block routes. We document both and include escalation phone numbers.
[05:35] Priya: Ok. For the A/B portion, we discussed live experiment at 10% vs 10% baseline—do we want to run that in the canary?
[05:45] Jordan: We recommend separating the A/B experiment from primary canary. Canary should validate infra and perf; A/B tests introduce feature-level variables. Better to run A/B after full cutover or as a separate canary with a narrower scope.
[06:06] Priya: Makes sense. We'll schedule the A/B following the go-live.
[06:12] Samir: Now the smoke tests — the runbook has 8 automated smoke steps: tokenization check, KV cache priming, 20 sample prompts across 3 seq lengths, cold start latency, streaming partials, function call routing, error-injection response (400/500), and end-to-end throughput baseline. They take ~18 minutes total.
[06:40] Michael: Can we run them in staging as a dry-run? Preferably next week.
[06:45] Samir: Yes, suggested dry-run date is 2025-06-30. I'll schedule and send invites.
[06:52] Priya: Please record the dry-run and share logs. We'll need them for our audit trail.
[06:58] Ava: We'll do that. Also on compliance: SOC2 docs are in the shared drive — security raised a question last week about KMS integration for private. Jordan, any update?
[07:10] Jordan: For Private deployments we support both customer-managed KMS and Redwood-managed keys. For Lumina we recommend customer KMS; runbook includes key rotation steps and HSM notes. We'll add a small KMS checklist for pre-cutover.
[07:30] Michael: Good. We'll need the KMS ARN and policy examples.
[07:35] Samir: I'll paste a sample policy in the runbook.
[07:40] Priya: On alerts — what thresholds will be paged vs paged as info? We want to minimize noise during the window.
[07:48] Samir: Critical alerts (pager) are error-rate breach >0.8% for 3 buckets, or 99th percentile latency >700ms for 3 buckets, or KV cache eviction >5% sustained. Informational: small latency upticks, minor SSR errors. We can tune thresholds for Lumina.
[08:10] Priya: Please set the initial alerts to be slightly wider — we can tune after staging.
[08:16] Samir: Noted; I'll set conservative thresholds for the staging dry-run and tighten for prod.
[08:22] Sofia: Who signs off for go/no-go?
[08:27] Ava: Sign-off matrix in the runbook: Lumina PM (Sofia) signs off on business readiness, Lumina Infra (Michael) on infra, Redwood SE (Samir) on technical health, and Redwood AE (Ava) coordinates. Execs can veto within the canary window.
[08:45] Priya: Ok. Any legal/procurement holds?
[08:50] Ava: Legal has cleared the contract addendum; procurement submitted SLA ack last week. I'll attach the signed doc in the runbook.
[08:58] Michael: One more network question — for private deployment will we do egress NAT from our VPC or route via private link?
[09:05] Samir: Prefer PrivateLink for less egress complexity, but runbook lists both options with pros/cons. PrivateLink requires some VPC peering steps which we've documented.
[09:18] Priya: Can you send the pros/cons page to our network team?
[09:22] Samir: Yes.
[09:25] Ava: Alright let's recap and lock owners. Action items: Ava to share runbook draft by Friday 6/27, Samir to prep staging dashboard and run smoke-test dry-run on 6/30, Michael to open firewall and share bastion creds by 6/26, Priya to confirm canary window by 6/26.
[09:48] Priya: Confirmed. Also we want Redwood to include a brief A/B test playbook as an appendix.
[09:55] Jordan: We'll draft an appendix and keep it separate from the core cutover doc.
[10:02] Sofia: Thanks everyone — can we sync again post-dry-run with logs?
[10:07] Ava: Yes, schedule a follow-up 24-48 hours after the 6/30 dry-run.
[10:12] Priya: Thanks.
[10:14] Michael: Thanks all.
[10:20] Ava: Meeting adjourned.

Notes about transcription: There are a few misheard product names (Redwood Dedicated sometimes transcribed as "Redwood Dedicatede") and acronyms (KMS sometimes captured as K-M-S), small timing punctuation errors. The transcript contains natural crosstalk near decisions and action-item assignment.

End of transcript.
